claim: When the gap between the buy and sell price on a currency's person-to-person board jumps to twice its own usual size, it is a short thin-market spike that closes again within hours.
calculation: From data/p2p_spread_signal.csv, one currency at a time, rows with a spread_ratio only. A spike starts at a row whose spread_ratio is at least 2 times the currency's own average when the currency's previous row with a ratio was under that, or it has none. The spike closed if a row of the same currency within 3 hours after the start has a spread_ratio under 2. A spike is judged only once it closed or the currency has a row at least 3 hours after the start. The figure is the share of judged spikes that closed.
window: spikes that started in the last 28 days of the file
min_observations: at least 10 judged spikes in the window
invalid_if: the finding's last recheck in data/findings.json is more than 3 days old, or the minimum observations are not met
thresholds_text: holds: at least half of the spikes closed within 3 hours. weaker: at least a quarter. no longer true: fewer than a quarter, which means a wide gap is a lasting state, not a spike.
trigger: new hourly spread rows (a spike is judged 3 hours after it starts)
proposed_by: Claude, 2 Nov 2026, from backlog 19a and SEB-49 (an Algeria spike that closed within three hours); the thresholds are proposals, merged by Seb's 20 Oct rule, and change only through a spec
